schema.description: Single source of truth for the Orbita CRM agent fields. The prompt's field dictionary, the output schema, the validator, the scorer, the review table, the permissions page, the record drawers and the CSV export are all derived from this file. Values are always stored as strings (or null); the type below says how a string is checked and normalised.
schema.seller_only_note: Deal amount, close date, probability, discount, price, contract term, owner and contacts are set by the seller only. The agent never proposes them; when the conversation asks for them, they go to ignored_out_of_scope.

levels.label: Always allow
levels.help: Written as soon as the update is prepared. You can undo it.

levels.label: Needs approval
levels.help: Proposed for your review; written only after you approve.

levels.label: Never
levels.help: The agent leaves this field alone.

fixed_rules: A proposal that contradicts a value you approved always waits for your decision.
The stage moves one step forward at most, and never to Closed Won or Closed Lost.
Amount, close date, probability, discount, owner and contacts are never written by the agent.

fields.label: Summary
fields.definition: What the conversation was about, the key facts and the outcome.
fields.evidence: Only facts stated in the transcript. No opinions or predictions.
fields.good: Intro call with the Commercial Director. Group and corporate requests arrive by email and live in spreadsheets, so requests get lost. He wants one place for every request and account, for 15 users, without a heavy implementation. A working session was agreed for 15 Oct.
fields.bad: Great call, the customer loved us and will probably buy. (opinion, not facts)

fields.label: Objections
fields.definition: Concerns, risks or blockers the customer raised in this conversation.
fields.evidence: A customer statement. Never the seller's speculation.
fields.format: 40 words max; several objections separated by '; '.
fields.good: Small, busy team; cannot take on a heavy implementation
fields.bad: Price may be an issue (when price was never mentioned)

fields.label: Commitments
fields.definition: Explicit promises made by either side in this conversation.
fields.evidence: An explicit 'I will' or 'we will'. Intentions such as 'maybe', 'we'll see' or conditional promises do not count.
fields.format: Party (person): action (by date); several commitments separated by '; '.
fields.good: Orbita (Ana): send the working-session agenda by 9 Oct
fields.bad: Customer will think about it

fields.label: Next step
fields.definition: The agreed next action or meeting that moves the opportunity forward.
fields.evidence: Agreed by both sides: proposed by one side and accepted by the other. A step the customer declined is not a next step.
fields.good: Working session with the Mar Azul sales coordinators on 15 Oct at 10:00
fields.bad: Second meeting with the team (when the customer said 'not yet')

fields.label: Follow-up owner
fields.definition: The Orbita person responsible for the next follow-up.
fields.evidence: That person says they will do it, or is explicitly assigned. Must be in the team roster; customer-side people are not allowed.
fields.format: Full name exactly as in the roster.
fields.good: Ana Ribeiro
fields.bad: Gustavo Teixeira (customer side) or 'Ana' (not the full roster name)

fields.label: Follow-up due date
fields.definition: The date by which the follow-up owner must act.
fields.evidence: An explicit date or day ('by Friday'), resolved from the conversation date. 'No rush', 'soon' or no timeframe means no evidence.
fields.good: Meeting on Tue 2026-10-06, 'by Friday' -> 2026-10-09
fields.bad: Inventing a date when the customer said 'no rush'

fields.label: Metrics
fields.ask: What number should the CRM move, and by how much?
fields.definition: The measurable result the customer expects from the CRM: the number they want to move, and by how much.
fields.evidence: A target or measure stated by the customer (a rate, a time, a count, money saved). A vague wish ('be more efficient') is not a metric.
fields.format: 40 words max; several metrics separated by '; '.
fields.good: Answer every group request within 24 hours; cut lost group bookings by half
fields.bad: Improve sales (no measure)

fields.label: Economic buyer
fields.ask: Who gives the final yes and owns the budget? Have we met them?
fields.definition: The customer-side person who gives the final yes and owns the budget for this purchase.
fields.evidence: That person says they decide or hold the budget, or another customer names them as the one who decides or signs. The speaker must be identified: a statement from an unattributed speaker does not establish who decides.
fields.good: Gustavo Teixeira (Commercial Director)
fields.bad: Ana Ribeiro (seller side) or 'the boss' (not a named person)

fields.label: Decision criteria
fields.ask: What will you judge the vendors on? What is a must-have?
fields.definition: What the customer will judge the vendors on: must-have capabilities and business or technical requirements.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer as a requirement or a deciding factor ('must', 'has to', 'a must', 'deal-breaker', 'we will choose on').
fields.format: 40 words max; several criteria separated by '; '.
fields.good: Shared view of group requests and accounts; follow-up reminders; light implementation
fields.bad: A good product (not a criterion)

fields.label: Decision process
fields.ask: What are the steps between today and the decision, and who is involved?
fields.definition: The steps and people that lead to the decision, in order: evaluations, validations and approvals.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer.
fields.good: The sales coordinators test it in a working session; then the Commercial Director decides
fields.bad: Standard process

fields.label: Paper process
fields.ask: Once you decide, what do procurement and legal need before the signature?
fields.definition: How the purchase gets signed once it is decided: procurement, legal, security or data reviews, contract and signature, and what could delay them.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer.
fields.good: Procurement asks for two quotes; Legal reviews the contract in two weeks; the Commercial Director signs
fields.bad: Paperwork (no steps)

fields.label: Pain
fields.ask: What goes wrong today, and what does it cost you?
fields.definition: The business problem that makes the customer act, in their terms: what goes wrong today and what it costs them.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer, or the seller's restatement confirmed by the customer.
fields.good: Group and corporate requests live in email and spreadsheets and get lost; the team needs one place for every request and account, with follow-up reminders
fields.bad: Interested in our product (not a pain)

fields.label: Champion
fields.ask: Who inside the company is pushing for this, and will they help us reach the economic buyer?
fields.definition: The customer-side person who actively sells Orbita inside the company and has influence on the decision.
fields.evidence: The person says they are pushing for the project or will win others over, or another customer names them as the sponsor. Enthusiasm alone ('I love it') is not enough. The speaker must be identified.
fields.good: Renata Lima (Sales Coordinator)
fields.bad: Ana Ribeiro (seller side) or 'someone in sales'

fields.label: Competition
fields.ask: Who else are you looking at, including keeping today's tools?
fields.definition: The alternatives the customer is considering for this purchase: other vendors, building in-house, or staying with what they have.
fields.evidence: Named by the customer.
fields.good: Northwind CRM; PipeSpark
fields.bad: Several vendors (not named)

fields.label: Seats (users)
fields.definition: How many people will use the CRM (licences).
fields.evidence: A number of users stated in the conversation. A range without a number the customer commits to is not evidence.
fields.bad: 600 (that is the company headcount, see employee_count)

fields.label: Departments
fields.definition: The teams that will use the CRM.
fields.evidence: Named in the conversation. A team clearly described counts ('my sales coordinators' -> Sales).
fields.format: One or more of: Sales; Customer Success; Customer Service; Marketing; Finance; Operations; Leadership; IT. Separated by '; ', in this order.
fields.good: Sales; Marketing
fields.bad: Front desk (not in the list)

fields.label: Integrations
fields.definition: Systems the CRM must connect to.
fields.evidence: Named by the customer.
fields.good: In-house booking system; email and calendar
fields.bad: Their systems

fields.label: Budget
fields.definition: The money the customer says is available for this CRM.
fields.evidence: Stated by the customer. A deal amount the seller is asked to record is an instruction about a seller-only field, not a budget.
fields.format: 'USD <amount or range> per <period>', for example 'USD 80,000-100,000 per year'; or 'No budget allocated' when the customer says so.
fields.good: USD 50,000 per year
fields.bad: USD 200,000 per year (taken from 'put us down for a two hundred thousand deal')

fields.label: Go-live target
fields.definition: When the customer needs the CRM live.
fields.evidence: A month or date the customer states as their target or deadline. 'Sometime next year' is not evidence.
fields.format: YYYY-MM (the month of the target or deadline).
fields.good: 'We need it live by March 2027' -> 2027-03
fields.bad: 2027-06 from 'sometime next year'

fields.label: Employees
fields.definition: Total number of employees at the client company.
fields.evidence: Stated in the conversation.
fields.bad: 15 (that is the number of CRM users, see seats)

fields.label: Current solution
fields.definition: What the client uses today to manage customers and deals.
fields.evidence: Stated in the conversation.
fields.good: Email and spreadsheets
fields.bad: Old system

fields.label: Stage
fields.definition: Sales stage of the opportunity.
fields.evidence: See the stage rules. Propose a new stage only when every exit criterion of the current stage is evidenced in this conversation.
fields.format: One value of the stage list.
fields.good: Qualified Opportunity (from New Lead, with a quote for each criterion)
fields.bad: Contract (from Proposal: more than one step)

transcripts.MTG-2001:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Good morning, Marina, Felipe. Thanks for making the time. Can you both hear me okay?
[00:00:06] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Loud and clear. Sorry we're a couple of minutes late, the traffic on the highway this morning was a nightmare.
[00:00:13] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): Same here. I left home at seven and I still barely made it.
[00:00:19] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): No problem at all, same for me, the usual Tuesday. So, the goal for today: you filled in our web form about a CRM, and I'd like to understand how your commercial team works today, what is not working, and whether Orbita is a good fit. Does that sound good?
[00:00:37] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Perfect. Let me give you some context. Acme is a freight and warehousing company, we're about eight hundred and fifty people, and around a hundred of them are in the commercial area.
[00:00:54] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And how does the commercial team manage customers and deals today?
[00:00:59] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): Honestly, spreadsheets and Outlook. Each rep has their own spreadsheet of accounts, proposals live on a shared drive, and everything else is in people's inboxes.
[00:01:16] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): When someone goes on holiday or leaves the company, we lose the history of the account. Last quarter we missed two contract renewals because nobody remembered the dates.
[00:01:32] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): And from my side, I have no visibility. Every Monday I ask for the pipeline and I get six different spreadsheets in six different formats. If this works, success for me is simple: zero missed renewals next year, and the Monday pipeline review done from one screen instead of six spreadsheets.
[00:01:57] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That's very common. Let me play it back to see if I got it right: you need one place where the whole team tracks accounts, deals and renewals, so nothing gets lost and you get a reliable view of the pipeline. Is that the need?
[00:02:14] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Exactly. One place for every account and every deal, with renewal reminders, and a pipeline I can trust on Monday morning. That is the priority.
[00:03:02] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Who would use the system day to day?
[00:03:07] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): The forty sales reps, our twelve account managers in customer success, and the leadership team, about eight managers, for the dashboards. So sixty users to start.
[00:03:25] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Sixty users, across sales, customer success and leadership. Got it.
[00:03:54] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): And the reps are on the road a lot, visiting warehouses and customers, so a mobile app is a must for them.
[00:04:07] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): What else does the system need to do on day one?
[00:04:12] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): Pipeline management, renewal alerts, email sync with Outlook so we stop copying emails by hand, and management dashboards for Marina.
[00:05:32] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): By the way, Felipe, did you send the photos from Saturday's barbecue to the group? My husband keeps asking.
[00:05:38] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): Not yet, tonight. Sorry, Ana.
[00:05:42] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): No worries. Now, about your systems: what would the CRM need to connect to?
[00:05:48] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Our transport management system, the TMS. It's ours, built in-house about ten years ago, and all the shipment data is there. We also use Orion ERP for invoicing.
[00:06:12] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): And to be honest, that is my main worry. I am concerned about integrating with our in-house TMS. Anything that touches operations during peak season makes me nervous.
[00:06:33] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): My worry is adoption. We tried a sales tool three years ago and the reps hated it. They went back to their spreadsheets in two months.
[00:06:54] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Both are fair concerns. On the TMS, we did a similar integration with an in-house system for another logistics client last year. I will send you that reference case by Friday, so you can see how we handled it.
[00:07:12] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): That would help a lot.
[00:08:22] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): On adoption, we usually start from the reps' daily routine: the mobile app, the email sync, and nothing they have to type twice. We can go deeper on that in a workshop.
[00:09:37] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Can I ask about budget? Is there money set aside for this project?
[00:09:44] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Yes. We have between eighty and a hundred thousand dollars a year for the CRM, licences and support included.
[00:10:12] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That's helpful. Are you looking at other vendors as well?
[00:10:18] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): We had a first call with Northwind CRM, and we're getting a demo from PipeSpark next week.
[00:10:29] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Good to know, thanks for being open about it.
[00:14:22] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): Ana, unrelated question: is your team going to the logistics trade fair in Joinville this year?
[00:14:29] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Probably, our marketing team usually goes.
[00:21:22] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Who else would be involved in the decision?
[00:21:28] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): I make the decision on this. It sits in my operations budget. But I will want our IT lead, Rui Tavares, to validate the technical side, the integration and the security.
[00:21:50] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And after Rui's validation, is there any other step? Procurement, legal?
[00:21:56] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Procurement needs three quotes for anything above fifty thousand. Then I sign.
[00:22:12] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And in terms of timing?
[00:22:15] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): We need it live before our peak season starts in April, so go-live by March 2027 at the latest.
[00:30:02] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): One more thing for the reps: we need to see each customer's shipment status inside the CRM, otherwise they will keep calling operations.
[00:30:16] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That comes back to the TMS integration, so it's a good topic for the workshop.
[00:35:02] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Proposed next step: a technical scoping workshop with Rui, the week of 9 November, to look at the TMS data and the integration options. Pedro, our solutions engineer, would join from our side.
[00:35:19] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Yes, let's do that. I will make sure Rui joins.
[00:35:25] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Great. I will send the workshop invite together with the reference case by Friday.
[00:41:42] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): And Ana, if you have a short video of the mobile app, send it over. I'd like to show it to two of our senior reps.
[00:41:50] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Sure, I'll include it in Friday's email.
[00:42:12] Felipe Nunes (Acme Logistics): For what it's worth, I'm the one who pushed for this project internally. If the mobile app is as good as it looks, I'll get the reps on board myself.
[00:42:40] Marina Lopes (Acme Logistics): Thanks, Ana. Talk soon.
transcripts.MTG-2002:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Hi Camila, thanks for taking the call on a Monday afternoon.
[00:00:05] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Hi Ana. Sorry if I sound tired, we're three weeks from Black Friday and the stores are going crazy.
[00:00:14] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): I can imagine. I'll keep it focused. You reached out about managing your franchise network, right?
[00:00:21] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Yes. We have thirty-eight own stores, but the growth is in the franchise and wholesale channel: forty franchisees and around two hundred wholesale buyers.
[00:00:39] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Today all of that runs on WhatsApp groups and spreadsheets. When a franchisee complains or a buyer asks for a reorder, it's lost in a chat somewhere.
[00:01:05] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): So what you'd want is one place where your team sees every franchisee and wholesale buyer, with their orders, visits and complaints?
[00:01:16] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Yes, that's exactly it. One place for the franchisees and the wholesale buyers, instead of fifty WhatsApp groups.
[00:02:35] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How big is Verde overall?
[00:02:39] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): About one thousand two hundred employees, most of them in the stores.
[00:04:10] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And how many people would use a CRM?
[00:04:15] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Honestly, I don't know yet. Maybe the regional managers, maybe more. I'd have to think about it.
[00:06:25] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): One thing I should tell you. Two years ago we bought a BI tool and it failed. It was too complicated and the store teams stopped using it after a month. I can't go through that again.
[00:06:47] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That's important to know. Simplicity would be a requirement, then.
[00:08:05] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Is there a budget for this kind of project?
[00:08:09] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Not right now. There's no budget allocated for this yet, it would have to go into next year's plan.
[00:11:25] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): By the way, my daughter started at the same school as your colleague's son, small world.
[00:11:31] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Really? That's funny, I'll tell him.
[00:16:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): We work with a fashion retailer with a franchise model very similar to yours. I'll send you our product overview and that case study.
[00:16:13] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Please do. I'll read it with my team after Black Friday.
[00:16:20] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Would it make sense to book a short demo for the end of November?
[00:16:26] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Let's not book anything yet. Send me the case study first and I'll come back to you. No rush, honestly.
[00:16:37] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Understood, no pressure.
[00:27:35] Camila Rocha (Verde Retail): Thanks Ana, have a good week.
transcripts.MTG-2003:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Hi Roberto, good morning. Pedro is with me. We wanted to go through the plan for Friday's demo with the clinic managers.
[00:00:11] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): Morning, both. I'm glad you called, because I have news, and it isn't good. The board froze all new IT projects until our budget review in January.
[00:00:30] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): I see. So Friday's demo...
[00:00:33] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): Please cancel the demo on Friday. There is no next step from our side for now, and nothing has been agreed beyond waiting for the budget review.
[00:00:55] Pedro Almeida (Orbita): Understood. Should we keep a placeholder in the calendar, maybe for December?
[00:01:02] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): No, please drop it. I can't commit to any date, not even a date to talk again.
[00:02:20] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): To be clear, the budget itself hasn't changed: it's still ninety thousand dollars a year. It's the timing that moved.
[00:04:30] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That's clear. Is there anything we can send that would help with the budget review?
[00:04:38] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): Not really. If the board approves the budget in January, I'll reach out to you.
[00:04:52] Pedro Almeida (Orbita): Thanks for being upfront with us, Roberto.
[00:08:20] Roberto Lima (Nimbus Health): Of course. I'm sorry about the timing. Take care, both of you.
[00:08:28] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): You too, Roberto. Thanks, bye.

[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Hi Livia, nice to meet you. Thanks for accepting the invite.
[00:00:06] Livia Prado: Hi Ana. A colleague recommended you, so I wanted to understand what you do.
[00:00:17] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Happy to explain. But first, tell me a bit about Delta Pharma.
[00:00:23] Livia Prado: We're a mid-sized pharmaceutical company. We have about one hundred and fifty medical representatives who visit doctors and pharmacies every day.
[00:01:08] Livia Prado: Their visit reports are in a very old system that nobody likes. I'm looking at options for next year.

[00:03:40] Livia Prado: Plan the visits, record what was discussed, and track samples. And it has to work on a tablet.

transcripts.MTG-2007:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Good morning, Sofia, Andre. Happy Friday!
[00:00:05] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Good morning, Ana. Happy Friday. Andre has just come back from a sales stand, so he has fresh stories.
[00:00:14] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): Plenty of them. We had three hundred visitors at the stand last weekend.
[00:00:25] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): That's a lot of leads. How do you capture them today?
[00:00:30] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): Paper forms at the stand, the website form, and WhatsApp. Then someone types everything into a spreadsheet on Monday, if they remember.
[00:00:56] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): And that's the problem. Leads get lost between the stand, the website and WhatsApp, and the brokers fight over who saw a client first.
[00:01:34] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): So the need is to capture every lead in one place and route it to the right broker?
[00:01:41] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Yes. Every lead from the website, WhatsApp and the sales stands in one place, routed automatically to a broker, with one sales funnel per launch.
[00:01:59] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Today a lead from the website waits about two days for a call back. I want every lead called within two hours.
[00:03:04] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How many people would use it?
[00:03:08] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): We'd need a hundred and five users: twenty-five in our own sales team and eighty brokers.
[00:03:23] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): And our marketing team runs the website and the campaigns, so they need to see where the leads come from.
[00:05:14] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): My concern is the brokers. They are not employees, and they won't use anything complicated. And the stands often have no mobile signal at all.
[00:05:35] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Our mobile app works offline and syncs when the signal comes back. I can show you that.
[00:07:09] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How big is Cedro today?
[00:07:13] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): About four hundred people, most of them on construction sites.
[00:09:24] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Have you set a budget for this?
[00:09:28] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): We have around sixty thousand dollars a year for it.
[00:12:04] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Who makes the decision on a project like this?
[00:12:09] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): I do. Our CEO only gets involved above two hundred thousand, so this is my call. Legal reviews the contract before I sign.
[00:12:34] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And timing?
[00:12:37] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): We have three launches next year, the first one in April. I need this running by March 2027.
[00:13:59] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Are you talking to other vendors?
[00:14:03] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Not yet, you're the first.
[00:20:44] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): For the funnel, we need to see each launch separately: leads, visits to the show apartment, proposals and contracts.
[00:31:34] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Here's what I suggest: I'll send you a recorded demo of the lead routing by Tuesday, and then we do a live demo with your sales managers on Thursday the 12th.
[00:31:49] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Yes, Thursday the 12th works for us.
[00:31:56] Andre Pires (Cedro Construtora): I will send you the list of the three launches and the broker teams before the demo.
[00:34:24] Sofia Martins (Cedro Construtora): Thanks, Ana. Have a great weekend.

transcripts.MTG-2009:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Good afternoon, Daniela, Marcos. Pedro is with me again. The plan for today is to agree the scope, so we can prepare the proposal.
[00:00:11] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Perfect. We blocked the full hour, so let's use it.
[00:00:19] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): And I brought my list of technical questions, as promised.
[00:00:28] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Great. Daniela, let's start with the users. Who would use the CRM?
[00:00:35] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Our admissions counsellors are our sales team, eighty of them across the six campuses. Marketing has twenty-five people running the campaigns. And fifteen managers in the leadership team need the reports. So one hundred and twenty users.
[00:01:15] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And how do the counsellors work today?
[00:01:20] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Each campus has its own spreadsheets, and a lot happens on WhatsApp. We have no idea how many prospects we lose between the first contact and the enrolment.
[00:01:45] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Our target for next year is to lift the conversion from first contact to enrolment from eight to twelve percent.
[00:03:05] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): What must the CRM do from day one?
[00:03:09] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Capture the leads from our campaigns, give each counsellor a follow-up list, show the enrolment funnel per campus, and keep the WhatsApp conversations with the prospect's record.
[00:05:35] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): On integrations, it has to connect to Campus One, our student information system, because that is where an enrolment becomes official. And to Mailwave, the email tool marketing uses.
[00:06:00] Pedro Almeida (Orbita): Both have APIs we've worked with. What about WhatsApp?
[00:06:05] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): Yes, WhatsApp too, through the official business account.
[00:09:25] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): My main concern is student data. It must stay in Brazil, and we need a data protection assessment before anything goes live.
[00:09:46] Pedro Almeida (Orbita): Our data centre for Brazilian clients is in São Paulo, and we can support the assessment.
[00:12:15] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How will the decision be made on your side?
[00:12:20] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): First an IT security review and the data protection assessment. Then Daniela signs, and the board approves anything above one hundred and fifty thousand dollars a year.
[00:12:45] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): On the paperwork, procurement will need your standard contract and the data processing agreement two weeks before the signature.
[00:13:35] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And the budget?
[00:13:39] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): We've approved between one hundred and ten and one hundred and thirty thousand dollars a year.
[00:15:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Are you evaluating other options?
[00:15:04] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): We're also looking at Clarion Sales Cloud. To be honest, they're cheaper, but their WhatsApp integration is weak.
[00:17:25] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): When does it need to be live?
[00:17:29] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): The enrolment campaign for the second semester starts in June, so we need it live by May 2027.
[00:24:05] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): Off topic, but did anyone watch the match last night? I still can't believe that penalty.
[00:24:11] Pedro Almeida (Orbita): Don't remind me.
[00:46:25] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): So the scope is clear for us: one hundred and twenty users across admissions, marketing and management, the Campus One and Mailwave integrations, and WhatsApp.
[00:46:43] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Please send us a proposal on that scope.
[00:46:52] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Will do. I'll send the proposal by Friday the 13th, and we can review it together on Tuesday the 17th.
[00:47:03] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Tuesday the 17th works.
[00:47:10] Marcos Antunes (Lumen Education): And I will send you our security questionnaire by Monday.
[00:51:35] Daniela Freitas (Lumen Education): Thank you both, this was very productive.
transcripts.MTG-2010:
[00:00:00] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Good morning, Paulo, Luiza. Can you hear me well? The connection from the countryside sometimes struggles.
[00:00:08] Customer (unattributed): We can hear you. We're in the meeting room at the head office today, the signal is good here.
[00:00:17] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Great. Tell me how the commercial side of Pampa Agro works.
[00:00:23] Customer (unattributed): We sell seeds and fertiliser through about two hundred dealers in the south, and our field reps visit them every week.
[00:00:58] Customer (unattributed): After each visit the rep fills in a paper report, and on Friday someone types it into a spreadsheet. We never know what a dealer ordered or what the rep promised.
[00:01:37] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): So the need is one place with every dealer visit, order and promise?
[00:01:44] Customer (unattributed): Yes. We need to know which dealer was visited, what they ordered and what was promised, in one place.
[00:03:13] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How many people would use it?
[00:03:18] Customer (unattributed): Thirty-two field reps in sales, and six people in the leadership team who want the reports. So thirty-eight users.
[00:04:33] Customer (unattributed): The problem is there's no mobile signal in the fields. Anything that needs the internet all the time won't work. And the reps are not used to apps.
[00:04:58] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Our app works offline and syncs later, and the visit check-in uses GPS.
[00:05:08] Customer (unattributed): Then it must work offline and have the GPS check-in, those two are non-negotiable.
[00:07:23] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): What systems would it need to talk to?
[00:07:27] Customer (unattributed): Our ERP is Orion ERP. The dealer orders need to flow there.
[00:09:03] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): How big is the company overall?
[00:09:07] Customer (unattributed): We're about four hundred and fifty people.
[00:12:33] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): Who decides on a project like this?
[00:12:37] Customer (unattributed): I make the final call on this, and I'm fine with the budget.
[00:12:48] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And what budget do you have in mind?
[00:12:53] Customer (unattributed): About seventy thousand dollars a year.
[00:13:23] Customer (unattributed): Between us, I'm the one pushing for this inside the company. The other directors still think paper works.
[00:14:13] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): And when would you need it?
[00:14:17] Customer (unattributed): Before the planting season sales in August, so live by July 2027.
[00:29:58] Ana Ribeiro (Orbita): I'll send you a short video of the offline mode by Monday. And would a field demo with two of your reps work next Wednesday, the 11th?
[00:30:11] Customer (unattributed): Yes, Wednesday the 11th works. We'll pick two reps.
[00:37:43] Customer (unattributed): Thanks, Ana. Talk soon.

expected.description: Expected results for the Call-to-CRM eval set (Orbita CRM, meetings from Granola). Each case starts from the seed CRM in data/opportunities.json and data/clients.json. Fields absent from a case are expected as no_evidence. status_any = several acceptable statuses; value / value_any compared by type; must_include = list of groups, every group must match and any keyword of a group is enough (case-insensitive); must_not_include = keywords that must not appear; note_must_include checks the field's note. 'unchanged' = the agent proposed exactly the approved value: nothing to decide, nothing written.

cases.name: Happy path - complete discovery call
cases.proves: A complete discovery call fills every field with a quote, and the stage moves only when the need, the decision-maker and the timeline are all on the call.

cases.name: No evidence - no follow-up date or further meeting agreed
cases.proves: When no date or next meeting is agreed, the agent leaves the due date and the stage empty instead of guessing, and records 'no budget' only because the customer said so.

cases.name: Contradiction with seller-approved values (short call)
cases.proves: When the call cancels an approved next step without agreeing a new one, the agent flags the conflict and lets the seller decide; a short call that ended normally is still usable.

commitment.note: Conditional promise; a proposal or no_evidence is acceptable.

cases.name: Unusable source - recording cut off mid-sentence
cases.proves: A recording that stops mid-sentence is blocked before the agent runs: no proposals and nothing to submit.

cases.name: New client - a meeting with a company that is not in the CRM
cases.proves: A conversation with a company the CRM does not know becomes a proposal for a new client and opportunity: nothing is created until the seller approves (or Settings allow it), and the fields are proposed like any other run.

cases.name: Stage boundary - 'let's sign' before the decision-maker has the proposal, spoken deal amount, stated budget
cases.proves: 'Let's sign' from someone who is not the decision-maker does not move the stage; a spoken deal amount is ignored while the stated budget is kept.

cases.name: Seller edits a proposal
cases.proves: The seller can rewrite a proposal: the CRM receives the seller's text and the record keeps both versions, who decided and when.

edit.customer_need: Capture every lead from the website, WhatsApp and sales stands in one CRM and route it automatically to the right broker, with one funnel per launch

platform_checks: The CRM receives the seller's edited customer need, not the agent's version
The activity record keeps both the agent proposal and the seller's final value
The activity record stores the reviewer (U01) and the decision time
Each written field records its write result (Succeeded)

cases.name: Access boundary - seller does not own the opportunity
cases.proves: A seller who does not own the opportunity sees nothing from it, and the attempt is logged.
platform_checks: No opportunity or client data is shown to U01
The access-denied attempt is written to the activity log

cases.name: Solution fit - scope session with every typed field; scope agreed and proposal requested
cases.proves: A scope session fills users, teams, integrations, competitors and go-live in valid formats, and the stage moves to Proposal only when the scope is agreed and a proposal is requested.

cases.name: Granola speaker attribution - customer voices without a name
cases.proves: When Granola cannot tell who is speaking, the agent still records the facts but does not name a decision-maker or move the stage on that statement.

cases.name: WhatsApp chat - terms agreed in an exported chat
cases.proves: A WhatsApp export is read like a meeting: it is attributed to the right opportunity by its contact, relative dates come from the message that says them, and the decision-maker's written yes plus the request for the contract move Negotiation to Contract.
